name: President Donald J. Trump International Airport (formerly Palm Beach International)

runway.v: the largest runway is 10,000 ft × 150 ft (about 3,048 m × 46 m); runways shown are 10L-28R, 10R-28L and 14-32

customs.v: CBP clears aircraft 7 days a week 09:00–19:00 (office hours 08:00–20:00 Eastern Time); contact CBP at least 4 hours before leaving the foreign port; FIS facility on its own ramp, not attached to an FBO or the terminal

hours.quote: The airport has a 24-hour control tower and a U.S. Customs & Border Protection port of entry facility.

handling.v: the County's general aviation page says three fixed-base operators but lists four names: Atlantic Aviation, Jet Aviation, Signature Flight Support and NetJets
handling.quote: has a choice of three fixed-base operators

noise.v: voluntary noise abatement procedures from a Part 150 study; no penalty for not using them; the page gives no hours or procedure details
noise.quote: there is no penalty for failing to utilize noise abatement procedures.

notes: Operator is the Palm Beach County Department of Airports; its site now names the airport 'President Donald J. Trump International Airport' (DJT); CBP's fact sheet (7 Mar 2024) uses KPBI. The voluntary night restraint could not be verified: pbia.org/noise redirects to https://flydjt.org/noise/ and that page, and https://discover.pbc.gov/airports/pages/noise-abatement.aspx, were blocked; the two Part 150 documents opened were for Lantana (LNA), not this airport. The CBP sheet gives no time zone on the 0900-1900 line; Eastern Time is given for office hours. KPBI is not in the US AIP AD 2 Florida page. ft to m conversion mine (1 ft = 0.3048 m). 1 Nov 2026: the County's Noise Abatement page (https://discover.pbc.gov/Airports/Pages/Noise-Abatement.aspx) now opens but only says the Noise Abatement Office enforces noise rules at the airport; it gives no hours or procedures. https://flydjt.org/noise/ could not be opened (permission request not answered). Nothing added. | 3 Nov 2026: IMPORTANT, the County's Name Change FAQs say the name changed on 9 Jul 2026, 'The ICAO identifier changed to “KDJT.”' and the IATA code changed from PBI to DJT on 18 Aug 2026; the FAA chart valid 29 Oct to 26 Nov 2026 (https://aeronav.faa.gov/d-tpp/2611/00449PALMBEACH.PDF) shows 'PRESIDENT DONALD J TRUMP INTL(DJT)'. This file is still named KPBI: the owner should decide on renaming. The Noise FAQ also says 'Airports in the United States are required to be open 24 hours a day and cannot restrict operations due to federal law.'; this is a general statement and does not name a curfew at this airport, so curfew is not recorded as none. The FBO list PDF (https://assets.simpleviewinc.com/simpleview/image/upload/v1/clients/pbi/DOA_Fixed_Base_Operator_List_3_19_24_9e736a13-c382-48f6-afcb-7e2ae080bee6.pdf) was not opened (permission request not answered), so FBO names stay missing. The Runway Use page and FAA Noise Regulations page have no night or voluntary hours. 5 Nov 2026: read https://flydjt.org/general-aviation/ (no date; footer 2026): FBO names added. It says three FBOs but lists four, including NetJets, so ask the County which three if it matters. The earlier handling rule's detail stays true to its own source (kpbi-pbc-airport): general aviation uses the south side and may not use the north ramps without the Department's approval. Runway Use page and CCAN minutes of 15 Dec 2022 have nothing on night hours. Not opened: FAA pilot handbook https://www.faa.gov/flight_deck/pilot_info/djt.pdf (permission not answered), Chart Supplement 29 Oct 2026 page (hand-built URL refused); 9 Jul 2026 pages 183 and 195 do not hold this airport. Slots: the FAA lists (Federal Register 9 Oct 2026; Level 3 page of Jan 2023) do not name this airport, but no source says so of it, so nothing is recorded. | 7 Nov 2026: read the FAA Flight Deck DJT page (last updated 21 Jul 2026: 'ATCT: Operates 24 hours') and the FAA DJT pilot sheet (https://www.faa.gov/flight_deck/pilot_info/djt.pdf, no date): neither mentions PPR, noise or night restrictions, weight limits or fuel. The old pbia.org GA page repeats the north-ramp restriction ('unless prior approval by the Department') and 'three full-service fixed base operators'. Nothing added. Failed: FAA Chart Supplement SE 29 Oct 2026 (https://aeronav.faa.gov/Upload_313-d/supplements/CS_SE_20261029.pdf, permission not answered). | 9 Nov 2026: read the FAA notice of proposed rulemaking 'Establishment of Special Air Traffic Rules in the Vicinity of President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT)' (Docket FAA-2026-10827, Notice 26-14, published 2 Sep 2026, https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-17957.pdf). It is a PROPOSAL, not a rule, so nothing is recorded: it would set a permanent Special Flight Rules Area of 1 NM radius, surface to 2,000 ft MSL, around Mar-a-Lago; arrivals and departures at DJT on an active IFR or VFR flight plan would be allowed, with two-way radio contact, ATC authorisation and a discrete transponder code; when the President is there, the FAA will keep issuing a TFR whose NOTAM controls. The preamble says it mirrors the current interim restriction (NOTAM FDC 5/2809, running to 20 Oct 2026). Check NOTAMs for any trip. Not opened (permission not answered): CBP fact sheet listing pages gave no KPBI/KDJT sheet. Curfew, PPR, fuel, max aircraft and slots still missing.
